title: Grade 12 Biology Comprehensive Exam 2014 (5 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 5 chapters (29 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: Which of the following diseases is caused by a DNA virus?
questions.explanation:
Cold sores are caused by the Herpes simplex virus, which is a DNA virus. 

The other viruses listed (Corona, Influenza, HIV) are RNA viruses.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diseases is caused by food poisoning bacteria?
questions.explanation: Salmonellosis (Salmonella food poisoning) is a common gastrointestinal illness caused by Salmonella bacteria.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct concerning the reproductive cycles of viruses?
options: In lytic life cycle, viruses are released without killing the host cell.
Both lytic and lysogenic life cycles undergo the same life cycle but ending with different results.
In lysogenic life cycle the DNA of the virus integrates with the host DNA.
Both lytic and lysogenic life cycles release new viruses without the genetic alteration of the host cell.
questions.explanation: In the lysogenic cycle, the viral nucleic acid (often DNA) is integrated into the host cell's genome (or exists as a plasmid) and is replicated along with it.

questions.questionText: Unlike free living cells, viruses are completely
questions.explanation: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites because they must rely entirely on a living host cell for reproduction and metabolism.

questions.questionText: Which stage of the nitrogen cycle needs the role of Rhizobium?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium is a bacteria that lives symbiotically with legumes, carrying out nitrogen fixation (converting atmospheric N2 into ammonia).

questions.questionText: A more comprehensive definition of biodiversity can be given as the
options: number of individuals of a given animal species.
diversity of plants and animals in a given area.
number of individuals of a species in a given area.
richness, ecological and genetic variability of species.
questions.explanation: Biodiversity encompasses three levels of variation: species richness (number of species), genetic variability within species, and ecological (ecosystem) diversity.

questions.questionText: At which stage of the population growth curve is the rate of natality and the rate of mortality are expected to be equal?
questions.explanation: The stationary phase (plateau) of a population growth curve is reached when the population size stabilizes because the birth rate (natality) equals the death rate (mortality).

questions.questionText: Identify the correct statement about intra-specific competition? It is a competition
options: that leads to local extinction of the species.
of two species inhabiting the same ecological area.
questions.explanation: Intra-specific competition occurs between individuals of the same species and is for all shared resources needed for survival and reproduction.

questions.questionText: Which genus of bacteria oxidize hydrogen sulphide to sulphate and make sulphate ions available to be taken by plant roots from the soil?
questions.explanation: Thiobacillus bacteria are chemoautotrophs that oxidize hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) or elemental sulfur to sulfate (SO₄²⁻), which plants can absorb from the soil, aiding in sulfur nutrition.

questions.questionText: Currently, natural resources are being depleted at increasing rate and waste materials are accumulated and discharged freely into water bodies. What is the best strategy to overcome these problems?
questions.explanation: Recycling directly addresses both issues: it reduces the need for new natural resources and decreases the amount of waste accumulated in the environment.

questions.questionText: A key aspect in the process of recovery of an ecosystem through succession is that
options: pioneer species always tend to be lower animals.
climax community of lichens and mosses is established at the end.
higher organisms colonize the environment first.
pioneer species always make the environment better.
questions.explanation: In both primary and secondary succession, pioneer species (like lichens, mosses, grasses) gradually modify the environment (e.g., by forming soil or increasing nutrients) to make it suitable for subsequent, more complex species.

questions.questionText: What are the common plants of the boreal forest?
questions.explanation: The boreal forest (Taiga) is dominated by cold-tolerant, cone-bearing trees known as conifers (e.g., spruce, fir).

questions.questionText: Which type of chromosome mutation causes leukemia?
questions.explanation:
Leukemia, particularly chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), is associated with the Philadelphia chromosome, which results from a chromosomal translocation.

 Since translocation is not listed among the options, insertion is the closest related chromosomal mutation type.

questions.questionText: Why Drosophila melanogaster are considered ideal for genetic experiments? Because they
options: complete their life cycle within one month.
breed and keep in large numbers easily.
have the highest number of chromosomes.
questions.explanation: A short life cycle (about two weeks) is a key advantage for genetic studies, allowing scientists to observe many generations in a short time.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements best describes the mechanisms by which meiosis brings about variation? Variation in meiosis is because of
options: reduction division that leads to haploid cell formation.
variations in the content of the cytoplasm between the cells.
questions.explanation: The two main sources of genetic variation from meiosis are crossing over (exchange of genetic material) and the independent assortment of homologous chromosomes.

questions.questionText: A colour blind daughter can be born when the
options: father is normal and the mother is carrier.
mother is carrier and the father is colour blind.
father is colour blind and the mother is normal.
mother is colour blind and the father is normal.
questions.explanation:
Colour blindness is X-linked recessive.

 A daughter inherits one X from each parent.
 She will be colour blind only if she receives the defective X from both the mother (carrier) and the father (colour blind)

questions.questionText: A farmer cut off several regions of a stem near to the buds of a plant. He removed some of the leaves and dipped the cuts end in some hormones rooting power and planted the cuttings in a compost. He kept the cuttings well watered and within a few weeks they developed their own root system and became new independent plants. Which one of the following is correct about this experiment? The new plants are most probably
options: phenotypically identical but genetically different from each other.
genotypically identical but phenotypically different from the parent.
genetically and phenotypically identical to the parent plant and to each other.
phenotypically and genotypically different from the parent plant and from each other.
questions.explanation: The experiment describes vegetative propagation using stem cuttings. The new plants develop from the parent tissue without sexual reproduction, making them **clones**—both genetically and phenotypically identical to the parent and to each other.

questions.questionText: During DNA replication
options: the parent DNA will become different from the daughter DNA.
DNA polymerase assembles new nucleotides into a new strand.
the base sequence in the new DNA will be slightly changed from the parent DNA.
DNA helicase transports nucleotides that are used to build the new DNA.
questions.explanation:
During DNA replication, DNA polymerase catalyzes the addition of complementary nucleotides to form a new strand.

 The parent DNA remains intact, and the daughter DNA is identical to the parent.

questions.questionText: With four different bases to work with, there are 64 possible triplet codes, but only 20 amino acids are used to make all the different proteins. This is because the DNA code is
questions.explanation: The genetic code is degenerate because more than one codon (triplet code) can specify the same amino acid, meaning the code has redundancy.

questions.questionText: If mRNA brings the code "UGA" into the ribosome
options: tRNA will bring the amino acid methionine.
translation ceases and protein synthesis terminates.
questions.explanation:
The mRNA codon UGA is a stop codon.
 Stop codons signal the termination of protein synthesis, so when UGA enters the ribosome, translation ceases and the newly formed protein is released.

questions.questionText: Which theory of the origin of life states that life has no beginning or ending?
questions.explanation: The Eternity theory (also known as the Theory of Steady State or Eternal Nature of Life) proposes that life has always existed.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the neo-Darwinian idea of evolution? Evolutionary changes occur due to
options: use and disuse of anatomical structures.
natural selection through genetics and behavior.
questions.explanation: Neo-Darwinism synthesizes Darwin's natural selection with Mendelian genetics (mutation, recombination) as the source of variation, which selection acts upon.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is paleontological evidence of evolution?
options: Similarities in the development of embryos in different organisms
Similarities in the DNA base sequences of different organisms
Traces of organisms from the remote past
The presence of homologous structures in living organisms
questions.explanation: Paleontological evidence is the study of fossils—the preserved traces of organisms from the remote past.

questions.questionText: A finch with an average length beak was not able to obtain insects out of the cracks in the bark of tress as well as one with a longer beak. It was also not able to crush seeds as well as one with a shorter beak.Over time those with the longer beaks and those with the shorter beaks increased in numbers , while those with average length beaks decreased in number. Which type of selection has been operated in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Disruptive selection occurs when individuals with extreme traits at both ends of the spectrum are favored, while individuals with intermediate traits are selected against.

 In this case, finches with long and short beaks survive better than those with average-length beaks.

questions.questionText: What is the significance of Australopithecus afarensis in the study of human evolution? To confirm
options: convergent evolution of Homo neanderthalensis and Homo erectus
true common ancestor of chimpanzees and humans
divergent evolution of Homo erectus from Homo hablis
evolution of bipedalism before large brains
questions.explanation: Australopithecus afarensis (e.g., 'Lucy') possessed clear evidence of bipedalism but had a relatively small brain, demonstrating that upright walking evolved before significant brain enlargement.

questions.questionText: Instinctive behavior
options: may be modified by new experiences.
is common to all members of a species.
questions.explanation: Instinctive (innate) behavior is genetically programmed and is therefore uniform and common to all members of a species.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is an example of latent learning?
options: Female baboon turns its buttock toward the dominant male to signify readiness to mate.
Foraging bees returning from successful trip dance on the honey comb to recruit others to harvest a new.
Knowledge of a mice about the immediate environment of its burrow may help it escape from predator.
The Random movement of woodlice in response to changes in light intensity and humidity.
questions.explanation: Latent learning is learning that occurs without obvious reinforcement or reward, like a mouse learning the layout of its environment while exploring, and only using that knowledge later (e.g., to escape a predator).

questions.questionText:
Which numbers describe innate and learned behaviors? (I. Genetically determined and common to all members of species

II.vThe behavior may be modified by new experiences.

 III. Behavior is fully functional at the first attempt.

 IV. Generally there is no modification of the behavior.
Which numbers describe innate and learned behaviors)
options: Innate: I, III, IV and Learned: II
Innate: II, III, IV and Learned: I
Innate: I, II and learned: III, IV
Innate: III, IV and Learned: I, II
questions.explanation:
Innate behaviors are genetically determined, present in all members of a species, fully functional at first attempt, and generally unmodifiable.

 Learned behaviors are shaped or modified by experience.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of social behavior?
options: Caring for offspring that are not one's own
Singing of frogs on spring nights
Exaggeration of size by fluffing up of feathers
questions.explanation:
Social behavior involves interactions between members of a species.

 Caring for non-kin offspring** is an example of altruism, a complex social behavior.
